findings.issue_text: Recovery-code validation accepts codes based only on membership in `generatedKeys` and never consumes the accepted code, allowing the same recovery code to be reused indefinitely.
The federated credential lookup may return empty, but the bean unconditionally calls `credentialModelOpt.get()`, causing a login-time `NoSuchElementException` for compatible user-storage providers.

goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

The golden comment specifically mentions RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) returning an Optional, and the candidate mentions 'credentialModelOpt.get()' being called unconditionally when the lookup may return empty. They're describing the same bug - unsafe Optional.get() call without presence check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery-code validation accepts codes based only on membership in `generatedKeys` and never consumes the accepted code, allowing the same recovery code to be reused indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java, the isValid method for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE (around line 295-310) only checks if the input code exists in the generatedKeys list using `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`. It never removes or marks the used code as consumed. This means the same recovery code can be validated successfully multiple times, which defeats the purpose of one-time recovery codes. The code deserializes the stored credentials, checks membership, but doesn't update the stored credential to remove the used code.
